correctness.rationale: Complete proof: direct cubic self-ambiguity reduces to imprimitive quadratic Gauss sums with exact zero iff p^{v_p(k)} does not divide modulation and magnitude p^{(a+v_p(k))/2} otherwise. A real impulse epsilon<=1 cannot cancel any nonzero branch (lower bound >=3); at zero branches exact nearest-root sine geometry yields the global minimum, attained with k=p. Weyl-diagonalization gives invertible lifted map and sharp condition number. Counting valuations gives unperturbed rank (pN²+1)/(p+1). Direct finite-sum checker passes for N=25,49,125 at epsilon=1 and .4; numerical finite tests only corroborate the all-order proof.

originality.rationale: Li (arxiv:2609.09614) Proposition 5.1 covers the vanishing of the unmodified cubic chirp, but does not state the sharp positive-one-impulse repair or count the associated prime-power matrix-lifting rank. General Gabor phase-retrieval and lifting criteria in Bojarovska--Flinth (arxiv:1503.05800) do not imply this exact prime-power construction or sharp margin. The closest published single-impulse result concerns a quadratic chirp and has fundamentally different pure-chirp ambiguity and a different conditioning law. Actual semantic searches of published result records for cubic/Alltop prime-power impulse aliases and explicit sine/rank parameters found no exact or broader covering statement. Older radar sequences remain a priority risk.
